text.p: Swiss bonds were firmer while the short end of the curve lagged in late trade.
Bonds in the longer end were boosted by cash buying, with one trader cited especially strong interest in the 4-1/2 percent April 2006 and 4-1/4 percent January 2008 federal bonds.

The trader said that Credit Suisse, and later Swiss Bank Corp, bought "massive material" in that sector late on Thursday and again on Friday. He said that the buying was also reflected in demand for the Dec Conf futures contract at 114.90 to 114.94, which was near the 114.99 day session high.
Traders were speculating that the purchases were either linked to short-covering, or adjustments in spread positions.

The tone in the long end was also helped by favourable demand for the U.S. Treasury's 30-year bond auctioned Thursday. The yield on the U.S. benchmark 6-3/4 percent 30-year slipped to an eight-month low of 6.54 percent on Thursday post-auction.
The Swiss curve continued to flatten as the franc's renewed declines, mainly versus the mark, took a toll on the short end.
In foreign bonds, traders said demand was favourable for recent offerings from Engadiner Kraftwerk SBHC launched November 6, and Argentina DSUC PBHG launched November 4.
Swiss traders said selling was seen mainly in the maturities up to four years.
The dollar lower than the 21-month highs it hit against the franc on Wednesday, trading back below 1.28 francs. But the mark rose to new 20-month highs on Friday, touching 84.37 Swiss centimes.

On Thursday evening, Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer told a business forum at a Swiss university that the SNB was "not unhappy" with the Swiss franc's latest declines, but also said that the currency's fluctuations could not be the sole focus of central bank policy.
